_comment: Phase 0 frozen operating baseline for the @odla-ai/chapter adoption. This file is acceptance authority: Chapter's resolved behavior is compared against it, and a difference is a defect until a PM decision records it as intentional. Captured 2026-07-25 from the deployed dev worker and the checked-out tree, NOT from memory or git history.

freeze.snapshotNote: Snapshot held OUT of the repo (member PII). Re-take with: npx @odla-ai/cli app export --env dev --fresh

naturalKeys.applications: id (uuidv7, mirrored as a unique attr); email is indexed but NOT unique because a person may reapply
naturalKeys.meetings: id; applicationId is the relation carrier
naturalKeys.emailLog: id; dedupeKey is the caller-stable replay key
naturalKeys.superAdmins: id AND email, both unique, keyed by lowercased email
naturalKeys.crm_record: id; matched to applications by email

rules.state: deny-all on every one of the 13 namespaces
rules.verified: confirmed mechanically against the deployed rules meta in the snapshot
rules.requirement: Chapter must keep default-deny; any namespace Chapter widens is a defect

application.disclaimerAck: legacy writes disclaimerAckAt when body.disclaimerAck === true, but does NOT reject a submit that omits it
application.profileProjectionNote: written to Clerk public_metadata.profile by ensureClerkAccount at submit time; the intro message stays db-only
application.submitIdempotency: client submissionId becomes mutationId join:<id> for server-side exactly-once

pipeline.paidTransition: the Stripe webhook flips submitted -> paid_pending_vetting; the webhook is the authoritative writer

auth.claimOrigin: Clerk publicMetadata.role; unknown or missing claim degrades to provisional
auth.superAdminsNote: read-only odla-db table; no worker route ever writes it, set only in odla Studio
auth.audAzpNote: CORRECTED 2026-07-26 per chapter-follower v7. The legacy verifier calls jwtVerify with { issuer } only and enforces neither aud nor azp. v7 is explicit: 'do not describe the absence of an aud or azp check as proof that authorization is complete' and 'record those cases as n/a, not as a security success'. An earlier report of this finding framed it as a clean parity/security result, which overstated it. The correct reading is narrow: because the reviewed existing policy does not enforce aud or azp, Chapter's issuer-only verification introduces NO REGRESSION, and there is no host verifier that must be preserved in front of Chapter. It says nothing about whether enforcing them would be better.
auth.escalationGuard: only super-admins may create or change an admin; self-demotion is blocked

refund.blockedReason: approved memberships are non-refundable per policy (409); already-refunded is 409
refund.mechanism: refund the earliest succeeded unrefunded charge, cancel the subscription; the status flip comes from the webhook

sends.adminNotificationNote: legacy fires adminNotification inside the Stripe webhook on first successful payment, NOT on submit
sends.replayGuard: emailLog.dedupeKey; a successful row means the mail went out

prices.note: the live Stripe Price is authoritative; provider-side amount/currency/interval equality is a cutover gate

scheduling.source: groups.schedulingJson; odla-db meetings is the source of truth, Google is the invite/Meet projection

emails.transport: Cloudflare Email Service via the SEND_EMAIL binding; falls back to log-only

clerk.accountNote: ensureClerkAccount runs server-side at submit, so the legacy account model is create, NOT none

CONTAMINATION_NOTICE.what: The deployed worker silver-and-salt-capital-dev is NOT running this branch's src/worker.ts. It serves Chapter built-ins (/api/config 200, /api/network/shared 401) and 404s legacy-only routes (/api/applications/count). It is a Chapter build deployed from another branch onto the SHARED dev tenant.
CONTAMINATION_NOTICE.how it surfaced: The canary returned 404 for /api/join-config where the dev worker returns 200. Root cause: this branch's legacy route is group-scoped (/api/groups/:id/join-config) and the flat path is Chapter's built-in name, so probing the deployment had taught the wrong route shape.
CONTAMINATION_NOTICE.what is STILL VALID: Everything derived from this branch's source (application fields and caps, pipeline stages and subsets, auth ladder, operations, sends trigger, account model) and everything read from the tenant DATABASE (schema, rules, row counts, group row). The tenant schema was independently verified to equal this branch's legacy source exactly, zero attribute differences, so the parity gate is sound rather than circular.
CONTAMINATION_NOTICE.what was CORRECTED: The route list below now comes from src/worker.ts in this tree, not from probing the deployment.
CONTAMINATION_NOTICE.what REMAINS SUSPECT: visualBaseline was measured against that other deployment's build. Public page geometry is likely unaffected (the HTML is the same static tree) but /join, /members/ and /admin/ may reflect the other branch's islands. Re-measure from a local build of THIS branch before using it for Phase 5 visual acceptance.
CONTAMINATION_NOTICE.confirmed independently: Only the three top-level labels were re-verified against src/app/admin/index.jsx in this tree. Labels are inventory keys, not behavior parity. src/app/admin/people-crm.jsx is the authoritative legacy People workspace evidence.

routes._source: src/worker.ts in THIS branch, read from source
routes.staticFallback: unknown /api/* returns JSON 404; everything else falls through to the ASSETS binding

visualBaseline.capturedFrom: deployed dev worker, iframe measurement harness
visualBaseline.horizontalOverflow: none at any width on any measured route

titles./join: Apply to Join | Silver & Salt Capital

visualBaseline.clerkContainment: confirmed rendering inside the site shell at 390 (email field + Continue + 'Secured by' + Development mode)
visualBaseline.KNOWN_GAP: The hidden-iframe harness did not mount the Clerk widget at 768/1280/1440, so the signed-OUT input/button counts on /members/ and /admin/ at those widths reflect the pre-Clerk shell only. Re-measure signed-out Clerk containment at those widths in a real viewport during Phase 5. This is a measurement limitation, not an observed layout defect.

sections: TRAINING MATERIAL (3 items, all COMING SOON)

authenticatedBaseline.INVALIDATED_INTERPRETATION: The three top-level labels match ChapterAdmin, but that did not make the replacement an information architecture no-op. The screenshot came from the contaminated Chapter deployment, while the reviewed legacy source mounted a custom People CRM with distinct summaries, exploration, role signals, tabs, and mutations. The source contract below is the acceptance authority.

peopleSourceContract.source: src/app/admin/people-crm.jsx at the frozen source commit
peopleSourceContract.acceptanceRule: Preserve this workspace through ChapterAdmin workspaces until each behavior is proven packaged-equivalent, deliberately composed, or accepted as a PM-recorded product change.

authenticatedBaseline.unauthenticatedApiGate: an /api/me fetch without the Clerk bearer token returns 401 {"authorized":false} while the page itself renders, confirming the gate is server-side

visualBaseline.regenerationNote: The public pages and app islands are static files in git, so the true 'before' is recoverable by checking out gitSha above and rebuilding. That is the authoritative before-record; these numbers are the fast comparison.
visualBaseline.TOOLING_CAVEAT: Owner-confirmed 2026-07-25: the Claude Code in-app browser pane renders these pages at a wrong height (content occupies only the upper portion of the stated viewport, and the dark header band clips short of the full width). The same pages are correct in real Chrome. Screenshots taken through that pane are therefore NOT authoritative for vertical geometry or visual acceptance, and an apparent height/banding difference there must not be filed as a visual regression. Use the measured numbers in this fixture (scrollWidth, computed font sizes, element boxes), which come from the page's own layout and were not affected, or verify in a real browser.

privacyHazard.note: dashboard.html, ecosystem.html, granola-inbox.js, newsletter-data.js, network/people*.js are gitignored local CEO tools present in the working tree
privacyHazard.requirement: the build copies git-tracked files only (git ls-files), never a recursive directory copy; Chapter adoption must not change this
